bib.title: AnimateDiff: Animate Your Personalized Text-to-Image Diffusion Models without Specific Tuning

read.skipped: Supplementary materials (training and inference configs, user-study details) are not in this PDF.

question: How can existing personalized text-to-image diffusion models be turned into animation generators without model-specific tuning?
hypothesis: A motion module trained once on video, with a domain adapter absorbing the video-quality gap, transfers to any personalized checkpoint sharing the same base T2I.
contributions: A pipeline that animates any personalized T2I without specific fine-tuning
Verification that a Transformer along the temporal axis is adequate for motion priors
MotionLoRA, a lightweight fine-tune adapting the motion module to new motion patterns
Evaluation on community models against academic baselines and commercial tools (Gen-2, Pika Labs), plus compatibility with controllable generation

method.summary: A temporal-Transformer motion module is inserted into an inflated Stable Diffusion v1.5 and trained on WebVid-10M with the image layers frozen, after a LoRA domain adapter is fitted to video frames to absorb the video-quality gap and then dropped (or scaled by alpha) at inference. MotionLoRA fine-tunes LoRA layers in the motion module's self-attention on 20-50 rule-augmented reference videos.
method.task: personalized text-to-image animation (text-to-video via module insertion)

datasets.name: WebVid-10M
datasets.preprocessing: Domain adapter trained on static frames randomly sampled from the videos

datasets.name: MotionLoRA reference videos
datasets.source: rule-based augmentation (zoom-in/out by shrinking/enlarging crop area over time)

datasets.name: Personalized T2I checkpoints from Civitai
datasets.preprocessing: Prompts built from each model's homepage trigger words

models.name: Stable Diffusion V1.5
models.architecture: latent diffusion UNet, four resolution levels

models.name: AnimateDiff motion module
models.architecture: temporal Transformer: self-attention blocks along frame axis, sinusoidal position encoding, zero-initialised output projection with residual

training.objective: epsilon-prediction MSE (Eq 2 for domain adapter on frames; Eq 7 for motion module/MotionLoRA on frame-wise latents)

other.stages: 1 domain adapter (LoRA in self/cross-attn, alpha=1), 2 motion module (adapter and base frozen), 3 optional MotionLoRA
other.note: Detailed configurations are in supplementary materials, not in this PDF

inference.decoding: iterative reverse diffusion from random noise, then decode latents; sampler not stated
inference.prompting: Prompts from each community model's homepage (trigger words)

parameters.domain_adapter_alpha: 1 in training; adjustable at inference, 0 removes it

other.controllable: ControlNet with depth map sequence, no extra training

metrics.name: User study Average User Ranking (Text, Domain, Smooth)
metrics.definition: participants rank results of the three methods on text alignment, domain similarity and motion smoothness; AUR

metrics.name: CLIP metric (Text, Domain, Smooth)
metrics.definition: CLIP scores; domain similarity computed between animation frames and reference images generated by the personalized T2I

eval.protocol: User study on animations from the same personalized T2Is; number of participants, prompts and models not stated in main text.

results.claim: AnimateDiff has the best motion smoothness in the user study.
results.setup: Animations from same personalized T2Is, ranking by participants, higher better
results.table: Table 1, row Ours, column User Study Smooth.

results.claim: AnimateDiff has the best domain similarity in the user study.
results.table: Table 1, row Ours, column User Study Domain.
results.note: Text2Video-Zero scores 2.620, higher than Ours 2.280, on user-study domain similarity

results.claim: On user-study text alignment AnimateDiff scores 2.210, marginally above Tune-a-Video.
results.table: Table 1, row Ours, column User Study Text.

results.claim: AnimateDiff has the highest CLIP smoothness and domain scores but the lowest CLIP text score.
results.setup: CLIP metric as in Wu et al. 2023 and Khachatatryan et al. 2023
results.table: Table 1, row Ours, column CLIP Metric Text.
results.note: CLIP Domain 87.29 and Smooth 98.00 are best (Table 1)

results.claim: MotionLoRA works with as few as 20-50 reference videos, 2,000 iterations and about 30M storage.
results.setup: Shot types (zoom, pan, roll) from rule-based augmented videos
results.quote:
MotionLoRA can achieve promising results even with as few as 20 ∼50 ref-
erence videos, 2,000 training iterations (around 1 ∼2 hours) as well as about 30M storage space
results.note: Unit of 30M not printed as MB

results.claim: With N=5 reference videos MotionLoRA degrades significantly; N=50 learns the pattern.
results.setup: Fig 7 qualitative, zoom-in; ranks 2 (~1M) vs 128 (~36M) comparable motion
results.quote:
when the number of
reference videos is excessively limited (e.g., N = 5), significant degradation in quality is observed

results.claim: A 1D temporal convolution motion module (matched parameters) yields identical frames with no motion, unlike the Transformer.
results.quote:
the convolutional motion module aligns all frames to be identical but does not
incorporate any motion compared to the Transformer architecture

results.claim: Lowering domain-adapter scaler from 1 to 0 improves visual quality and removes the WebVid watermark.
results.quote:
as the scaler of the adapter decreases, there is
an improvement in overall visual quality

limits: Quantitative evidence is a user study and CLIP scores against two adapted baselines; commercial tools compared only qualitatively (Fig 5).
User study size, prompts and CLIP details are in supplementary, not in this PDF.
AnimateDiff has the lowest CLIP text score and Text2Video-Zero beats it on user-study domain similarity.
Motion module tied to the base T2I (SD v1.5) of the personalized checkpoints.
Authors note misuse risk: generates human-related content and community models may contain inappropriate content.

terms.definition: LoRA layers fitted to static video frames to absorb the visual quality gap, dropped or scaled by alpha at inference
LoRA layers added to the motion module's self-attention to adapt it to new motion patterns

lineage.work: High-resolution image synthesis with latent diffusion models (Stable Diffusion)
Adding conditional control to text-to-image diffusion models (ControlNet)

figures.caption: Training pipeline of AnimateDiff. AnimateDiff consists of three training stages for the corresponding component modules.

figures.caption: Quantitative comparison. A higher score indicates superior performance.
